chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Murādī, who said:

I said to Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام: A man has boils and sores, so his skin and his clothes are filled with blood and pus, and his clothes are in the same condition as his skin. He said: “He prays in his clothes, and there is nothing upon him, and he does not wash them.”

key_terms.الدَّمَامِيلُ: boils or eruptive swellings on the body
key_terms.ثِيَابِهِ: his garments in which he prays
key_terms.دَمًا: blood present on the body or clothing
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no blame or liability upon him
key_terms.لَا يَغْسِلُهَا: he is not required to wash them

ai.seo_question: Can a person with continual blood and pus from boils pray in clothes stained with impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person afflicted with boils and sores whose clothing is continually soiled with blood and pus. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that such a person may perform salat (prayer) in those clothes without liability and is not required to wash them.
